name: Pork Pot-Pie
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: pieces of ribs of lean salt pork
ingredients.originalText: pieces of ribs of lean salt pork

ingredients.name: a slice or two of the fat of salt pork
ingredients.originalText: a slice or two of the fat of salt pork
ingredients.quantityText: a slice or two of the fat of salt pork

ingredients.name: one pint of sour or buttermilk
ingredients.originalText: one pint of sour or buttermilk
ingredients.quantityText: one pint of sour or buttermilk

instructions.text: Take pieces of ribs of lean salt pork, also a slice or two of the fat of salt pork.
Scald it well with hot water so as to wash out the briny taste.
Put it into a kettle and cover it with cold water, enough for the required want.
Cover it and boil an hour, season with pepper.
Add half a dozen potatoes cut into quarters.

When it all commences to boil again, drop in dumplings made from one pint of sour or buttermilk, two eggs well beaten, a teaspoonful of salt, a level teaspoonful of soda dissolved in a spoonful of water and as much flour as will make a very stiff batter.
Drop this into the kettle or broth by spoonfuls, and cook forty minutes, closely covered.

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Take pieces of ribs of lean salt pork, also a slice or two of the fat of salt pork.
2. Scald it well with hot water so as to wash out the briny taste.
3. Put it into a kettle and cover it with cold water, enough for the required want.
4. Cover it and boil an hour, season with pepper.
5. Add half a dozen potatoes cut into quarters.
6. When it all commences to boil again, drop in dumplings made from one pint of sour or buttermilk, two eggs well beaten, a teaspoonful of salt, a level teaspoonful of soda dissolved in a spoonful of water and as much flour as will make a very stiff batter.
7. Drop this into the kettle or broth by spoonfuls, and cook forty minutes, closely covered.
